answer: In an agent market trading pigment and saffron, each identity must lock a fixed bond for 90 days before it can vote on shared spending, and each bond buys one vote. A pulse of fake accounts gains no free influence: controlling 1,000 votes requires locking 1,000 bonds. The attacker must supply that capital and forgo its use for the full lock period, so creating more names does not make the attack cheaper.
